title: Manual Handling — Moving Kegs & Casks
blurb: Using T.I.L.E. and good lifting technique to move kegs and casks without hurting your back.
siteNotes: Where the sack barrows, keg trolleys and any lifting aids are kept (your manager will show you).
Which cellar ramps, drops, hatches and steps need extra care, and how they are lit.
Who to ask for a two-person lift on each shift.
legalNotes: Avoid hazardous manual handling where reasonably practicable, assess what cannot be avoided, and reduce the risk: Manual Handling Operations Regulations 1992. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1992/2793
T.I.L.E. (Task, Individual, Load, Environment) is the framework HSE uses for manual handling assessment.

CHECK: the trainer says musculoskeletal injuries account for "roughly a third" of workplace ill-health "across the UK". HSE figures for work-related ill-health have put musculoskeletal disorders at around a quarter to a third in recent years; please confirm the current figure before relying on it. The slides say "about a third", as the trainer does.

CHECK: the trainer says a full 50-litre keg "can weigh over 70kg". A full 50-litre keg is commonly nearer 60 to 65kg including the keg itself, depending on the keg. Please weigh a full one and confirm; the safe message (it is too heavy to throw around) does not change.

cards.title: Manual Handling: Moving Kegs & Casks
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- use T.I.L.E. before you lift
- lift with good technique and the right equipment
- keep the cellar clear and ask for help when a load is too heavy

cards.title: A busy cellar is a real back risk
cards.body:
Bad backs are one of the most common reasons people take time off work. Musculoskeletal injuries account for roughly a third of all workplace ill-health.

In a cellar full of heavy kegs that is a real risk. A full 50-litre keg can weigh over 70kg, which is far too much to be throwing around without thinking.

items.label: of thinking prevents a lot of injuries

cards.title: T.I.L.E.
cards.body: Before you lift anything, run through T.I.L.E. in your head. Ten seconds of thinking prevents a lot of injuries.

items.title: Task
items.text: What am I moving and where to?

items.title: Individual
items.text: Am I fit to do this? Do I need help?

items.title: Load
items.text: How heavy and awkward is it?

items.title: Environment
items.text: Is the floor wet, the ramp clear, the light good?

cards.title: Good technique
cards.body:
Get close to the load, bend your knees rather than your back, keep your back straight and lift smoothly.

Never twist while you are carrying weight. Move your feet instead.

items.title: Get close
items.text: Stand right next to the load.

cards.title: Do not be a hero
cards.body:
For full kegs, use a sack barrow or keg trolley, or get a colleague to help with a two-person lift.

Kegs can also be rolled or walked, but always slowly and in a controlled way so one never gets away from you.

left.title: Do
items: Use a sack barrow or keg trolley
Stop and get help if it feels too heavy

right.title: Do not
items: Roll them fast to save time
Struggle on with an awkward load

cards.title: Keep it clear, dry and lit
cards.body:
Keep cellar drops, ramps and hatches clear, dry and well lit, and take your time on the steps. If something feels too heavy or awkward, stop and get help.

> Protecting your back today keeps you working pain-free for years to come.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Run through T.I.L.E. before you lift
- Bend your knees, keep your back straight and lift smoothly
- Never twist: move your feet
- Use a sack barrow or keg trolley, or a two-person lift, for full kegs
- If a load feels too heavy or awkward, stop and get help

cards.q: What do the letters T.I.L.E. stand for?
cards.why: T.I.L.E. is the check you run through in your head before lifting: the Task, the Individual, the Load and the Environment.

cards.q: Roughly what proportion of workplace ill-health is musculoskeletal injury?
cards.why: Musculoskeletal injuries account for roughly a third of workplace ill-health.

cards.q: A full 50-litre keg can weigh over 70kg.
cards.why: A full 50-litre keg is heavy enough that you should never throw it around without thinking.

cards.q: When lifting, you should bend your...
cards.why: Bend your knees rather than your back, keep your back straight and lift smoothly.

cards.q: It's fine to twist your body while carrying a heavy keg.
cards.why: Never twist while carrying weight. Move your feet instead.

cards.q: Which one piece of equipment helps move a full keg safely?
options: A wheelie bin on its side
A sack barrow or keg trolley
cards.why: For full kegs use a sack barrow or keg trolley, or get a colleague to help with a two-person lift.

cards.q: Kegs should be rolled quickly so they do not slow you down.
cards.why: Kegs can be rolled or walked, but always slowly and in a controlled way so one never gets away from you.

cards.q: How should you change direction while carrying a load?
cards.why: Never twist while carrying weight. Move your feet instead.

cards.q: If a load feels too heavy or awkward, you should stop and get help.
cards.why: Stop and get help. Protecting your back today keeps you working pain-free for years.

cards.q: What should you check about the cellar 'Environment' before a lift?
options: The keg is the brand we usually stock
The floor and ramp are clear, dry and lit
The delivery note has been signed
The bar upstairs is quiet for now
cards.why: The Environment part of T.I.L.E. asks whether the floor is wet, the ramp is clear and the light is good.
